annotation.title_clean: Stereotyping of Social Robots in Eldercare: An Explorative Analysis of Ethical Problems and Possible Solutions
annotation.title_en: Stereotyping of Social Robots in Eldercare: An Explorative Analysis of Ethical Problems and Possible Solutions
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Weßel, M.; Ellerich-Groppe, N.; Schweda, M.
annotation.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, Vol. 335 (IOS Press)
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper offering an explorative principlist ethical analysis of gender stereotyping in social robots for eldercare. It maps problems and conflicts and discusses solutions for culturally sustainable social robots in pluralistic late-modern societies. Only the abstract is available.
key_provisions_or_claims: Gender stereotypes in human-robot interaction may be used strategically to optimise care outcomes.
Diversifying gender roles and needs among older people make stereotypical robot design ethically problematic.
Applies a principlist approach to map ethical problems and conflicts.
Discusses solutions for culturally sustainable eldercare social robots.
